newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Julon gets 20 million marks EBRD loan.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Julon gets 20 million marks EBRD loan.

text.p: Slovenian artificial fibres producer Julon said on Tuesday it had received a 20 million marks ($11.8 million) loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
Julon, majority owned by Italian group Bonazzi, said half the amount would be invested in modernising its production, while the rest would go towards increasing the company's equity.
"We chose an EBRD loan because its interest rates are much more reasonable than those offered on the Slovenian market," Damjan Kosmac, Julon financial manager told Reuters.
The interest rate on the loan is three percent over LIBOR and should be payed off in seven years time.
In 1995 the company received a capital injection of 35 million marks from the EBRD under the same conditions. Both loans will be payed off in 2003.
In 1996 Julon broke out of the red and its net profit climbed to two million marks, up from a loss of one million marks in 1995.
"We can attribute our rise in profit to rationalisation and modernisation of our production. I think 1996 profit could be even higher if investment was not so high," Kosmac said.
He said that Julon's investments in the past two years reached about 50 million marks.

The company's sales in 1996 rose to 78 million marks from 50 million and are forecast to reach 100 million in 1997, but the company does not expect a corresponding increase in its profit as it plans to establish reserves for paying off the debt.
